text.p: Italian bonds and Btp futures ended firmer but off new record highs seen early on in the session. Traders said European debt markets seen under a bit of pressure from the U.S. but sentiment remained fairly bullish. The lira was firmer against the mark.
"It was a pretty sloppy session," one London trader said.

After starting easier on profit-taking, the Italian market rose after a surprise Bank of Spain cut in its key money market rate. European markets were further boosted after the Buba's Krupp said weakness in Germany's economy should not be ignored, boosting hopes for an easing in German monetary policy.
The March Liffe Btp contract touched a new record high of 131.35 before slipping back.
But prices came off late in the session as U.S. Treasuries erased small gains after the Philadelphia Fed Jan index came in at 11.3, higher than forecast.
However, although the market was keeping a close eye on U.S. debt markets, some Milan traders said the Italian market was more closely following other European exchanges.
They noted U.K. gilts ended higher after December retail price inflation fell back and rates were left unchanged.
Italian cash bonds were steady in the wake of futures.
